definition: favouring your own located in whose harm is counted, never in whose value is raised

settled:
My framework adds no value multiplier for kin, friends or community. Favouring your own never raises anyone's sentience weight. Whatever an individual's multiplier is, it is a fact about them, and no relationship and no circumstance adjusts it.

Partiality is real all the same, and it sits entirely in whose harm gets counted rather than in whose value counts more.

Forcing a parent not to save their child inflicts a genuine non-consensual harm on that parent, in their own local value stream. No shared self is involved. That harm carries the consent weighting like any other, which raises the bar on when overriding a rescue is permitted.

The child's value is not raised. The parent's own harm is added to the ledger.

So an adoptive parent, with no relatedness and a full bond, is fully licensed to favour their child, and an estranged biological parent is not.

title: How Partiality Enters Without Unequal Worth
